title: Wolstenholme Primes and the Mod 4 Question

problemStatement.formal: Study whether there exists a Wolstenholme prime p with p congruent to 1 modulo 4.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize Wolstenholme primes, the two known examples, and the open mod 4 question.
whyMatters: Connects binomial congruences to computational number theory
Records the mod 4 behavior of the known Wolstenholme primes without closing the open question

proven: Small primes 5 through 23 are proved not to be Wolstenholme primes.
The two known Wolstenholme primes, 16843 and 2124679, are formalized and both are 3 mod 4.
Any third Wolstenholme prime must exceed 10^9, using an axiomatized literature search result.
open: Whether any Wolstenholme prime is 1 mod 4 remains open.
Whether infinitely many Wolstenholme primes exist remains open.
knownResults.goal: Record the completed axiomatized formalization of the Wolstenholme prime mod 4 question.

currentState.focus: Completed axiomatized source-backed record: primary proof has 262 lines, 30 theorems, 5 definitions, 3 axioms, and 0 sorries.

insights: Both known Wolstenholme primes are 3 mod 4.
The open question is equivalent to refuting the all-known-pattern conjecture that every Wolstenholme prime is 3 mod 4.
The large binomial computations are axiomatized rather than kernel-normalized.
mathlibGaps: Large binomial coefficient verification is not practical inside the Lean kernel for the known Wolstenholme primes.
